clue.text: Doorman's delivery?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a nightclub heavy who keeps unwanted people out
second meaning: in cricket, a short-pitched ball that rears up at the batsman

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive makes it read as something a doorman delivers; the 's simply means 'is'. In cricket, a bowled ball is a delivery, and a short one that rises sharply has its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a club's door attendant who ejects troublemakers and a fast, short-pitched cricket ball.

clue.text: First to bid, reckless and cocky

indicators.note: the first of the following word is all we keep, its opening letter alone

parts.note: rash means reckless, acting without thought

explanation.surface: A bold auction bidder jumps in first, rash and over-confident.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone brash is self-assertive and overconfident, which is what cocky describes.

clue.text: Free ale — shun rum

indicators.note: rum as an adjective means odd or strange, so the letters before it come out in a strange order

explanation.surface: An offer of free beer, with a temperance plea to avoid spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink to be avoided, but it is the adjective meaning peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: To unleash is to let loose or release, so it works as the verb free.

clue.text: In a stupefied state, Tom will need a pick-me-up later

indicators.note: later says the following piece comes after the first in the line of letters

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a + tonic, a restorative drink or medicine

explanation.surface: A dazed man called Tom will want a reviving drink later on.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom reads as a man's name, but a tom is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Catatonic describes a trance-like, unresponsive condition, so it means being stupefied.

clue.text: What it tends to do if the weather's beastly?

definitions.text: What it tends to do if the weather's beastly?

parts.words: What it tends to do if the weather's beastly?
parts.note: surface reading: what usually happens in nasty weather
setter's reading: beastly taken literally, weather full of animals, the idiom for a downpour

explanation.walkthrough: Beastly weather is normally just foul, but read literally it suggests animals falling from the sky, which is the idiom for very heavy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes torrential rainfall, the kind of heavy downpour typical of truly foul weather.

clue.text: Draw game with Italian painter

parts.note: a drawn match is a tie
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: A drawn match featuring an Italian artist among the players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests sketching, apt beside a painter, but it is a drawn result.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was an eighteenth-century Venetian painter famed for ceiling frescoes.

clue.text: Novel — name the one a Brit translated

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so the letters are converted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A quiz request to name the novel a British translator worked on.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Jerome K. Jerome's comic 1889 novel about a boating trip on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a famous English comic book, so it is an example of a novel.

clue.text: Fair, Shergar's opening odds

parts.note: even means fair, equal on both sides

indicators.note: an opening is the very start, so only the first letter of the horse's name is used

explanation.surface: A betting note that the racehorse Shergar started at fair odds.
explanation.walkthrough: Shergar was a famous Derby-winning racehorse, so 'opening odds' reads as a starting price, but only his initial is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens is the betting price where the stake is matched exactly by the winnings, a type of odds.

clue.text: Work in one, on view

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An artwork displayed as a single piece, now on view to the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal but is simply a piece of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A view in the sense of a belief or judgement is exactly an opinion.

clue.text: Too quick a shot, very out of the ordinary

indicators.note: something out of the ordinary is unusual, so the letters are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: A rushed shot at goal or target, quite unusual for the player.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhasty means acting with too much speed and too little care, the sense of too quick.

clue.text: Earmark for tax returns after first of April

indicators.note: after places the reversed piece behind the single letter
first of means only the opening letter of the next word is taken
something that returns comes back the way it went, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a toll is a charge or levy

explanation.surface: Setting money aside for tax returns that are due in April.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax returns' reads as the annual paperwork, but returns is a reversal signal acting on a word for tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to assign or set aside for a purpose, the verb sense of earmark.

clue.text: Grim realities for a Hebrew?

indicators.note: grim suggests something harsh and twisted, so the letters are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: Asks whether harsh facts of life are the lot of a Hebrew.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israelite was a member of the ancient Hebrew nation, so the two terms are equivalent.

clue.text: Anguish in the middle each is suffering

parts.note: the heart of something is its centre

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way and knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pain at the centre that every person in the group feels.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is deep emotional pain or grief, a close synonym of anguish.

clue.text: Well-loved Wodehouse character, reportedly a forger?

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so we want a word that is pronounced the same as the character's name

parts.note: P. G. Wodehouse's Psmith, whose P is silent, is said the same as a plain common surname

explanation.surface: Asks if a favourite P. G. Wodehouse hero was secretly a counterfeiter.
explanation.walkthrough: Psmith insists his P is silent, so saying his name gives a common surname. 'Forger' suggests a counterfeiter, but here it is one who forges metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith is a metalworker who shapes iron at a forge, so is literally a forger of metal.

clue.text: Where to find play's backroom boys?

definitions.text: Where to find play's backroom boys?

parts.words: Where to find play's backroom boys?
parts.note: surface reading: where to locate the unseen helpers of any enterprise
setter's reading: the stagehands of a theatre production, working out of sight of the audience

explanation.walkthrough: Backroom boys are people working out of view; in a theatre they literally work behind the stage scenery. The phrase also means out of public view generally.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the backstage area of a theatre and, figuratively, any work done privately away from public gaze.

clue.text: Drew bream cooking in pan

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone named Drew frying a bream fish in a pan.
explanation.walkthrough: The pan looks like a frying pan for the fish, but it is a warming pan: a lidded metal pan of hot coals once used to heat beds.
explanation.definitionFit: A warming pan, filled with embers and slid between sheets, was a traditional device for heating a bed.

clue.text: Humbly, top worker is going round home

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the joined words wrap around the word for home

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: Humbly, a senior employee walks around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top worker' reads as a boss, but it splits into two separate words placed either side of the home word.
explanation.definitionFit: Going somewhere cap in hand means approaching humbly and deferentially, as when begging a favour.

clue.text: Mad Tory practice upset Republican's opponents?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A crazy Conservative habit has angered the Republicans' rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party, a fitting decoy beside American politics.
explanation.definitionFit: In US politics the Democrats are the main rival party to the Republicans.

clue.text: Deer can't jump, lacking power, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly signals an unexpected outcome, so the remaining letters land in an unexpected order
lacking means going without, so that letter is removed

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged, ignoring the apostrophe
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A deer that, oddly, has no strength to leap.
explanation.definitionFit: The muntjac is a small Asian deer, now common in English woodland, so it is a kind of deer.

clue.text: Philosopher brought up in Marseilles, surprisingly

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means lifted from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
in says the letters sit inside the following words, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the city name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A philosopher who was, unexpectedly, raised in the French port city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' looks like an anagram signal, but it supplies the second half of the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertrand Russell was a leading British philosopher and logician of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Nina playing leading character in Evita, a musical

indicators.note: playing suggests the name is played around with, so its letters move
the leading character of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

explanation.surface: An actress called Nina takes the title role in the Lloyd Webber show Evita.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading character' suggests the star role, but it means a first letter. 'Evita' looks like the musical, yet the answer is a different show.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie is the Broadway stage show about a red-haired orphan, so it is an example of a musical.

clue.text: Mistake made by rascal blowing top

indicators.note: blowing the top means losing the uppermost part, which in a down entry is the first letter

parts.note: a terror is a naughty, unruly child

explanation.surface: A blunder committed by a scoundrel losing his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blowing top' reads as losing one's temper, but it removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Is doing as ordered leading to identification of illness

indicators.note: ordered here means put into a new order, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Following the doctor's orders helps pin down what illness you have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing as ordered' reads as obedience, but ordered is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagnosis is a doctor's determination of the disease a patient has.

clue.text: Lute, one carried by celebrity

indicators.note: something carried by another is held within it, so one piece goes inside the other

explanation.surface: A lute belonging to a famous musician, carried by them on tour.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is an Indian long-necked plucked string instrument of the lute family.

clue.text: Chief steward in rank bad mood

indicators.note: bad means spoilt or damaged, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: The head steward is in a foul temper, maybe annoyed about status.
explanation.definitionFit: A major-domo is the head servant running a large household, i.e. a chief steward.

clue.text: A doctor's about right to use preventive measures

definitions.note: a paraphrase of the verb: to ward off something by acting first

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A doctor is roughly justified in taking precautions against illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About right' reads as approximately correct, but about is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert something is to prevent or ward it off, which is what preventive measures achieve.

clue.text: Discs bringing unsurpassed performances

definitions.meaning: second meaning: best-ever results, as in world bests

explanation.surface: Hit discs produced from some outstanding performances.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both gramophone discs and best-ever achievements, as in breaking world bests.

clue.text: Small child in red, told off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A little one dressed in red gets scolded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Told off' reads as scolded, but off is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddler is a young child just learning to walk, so it is a small child.
